terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: For likeness work, solve the reference camera (forge/stage1_intake/solve_camera_pose.py) so the review render aligns with the photo and the reference can be projected. Confirm by overlay review.

objectClass.notes: Static monumental landmark building, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: a prop kit is only ever looked at from outside, so an interior costs draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. A Chinese-Thai neighbourhood shrine hall. A pale stone plinth carrying a tripod censer; a solid red-lacquer body with an open colonnade along its long face; seven round red columns on stone drum bases, of which the two centre ones are wrapped in gilt dragons; eleven conical incense coils hung across the open front; and over all of it a heavy low green-glazed hip roof, concave in section, with upswept curled ridge ends, four flying eaves corners and a pair of guardian beasts on the ridge.

reasoning: The registry notes open with a WARNING rather than a description -- it must not be built with the profile of a Thai wat -- so the roof is the whole problem: heavy, low, hipped on all four sides, concave in section and finished with strongly upswept curls.

That roof cannot be extruded or lathed. It is generated as a ring of eight-point rectangles climbing from the eaves to the ridge, which is the only one of the shape helpers in this batch that had to be written for a single asset.
The two features the notes call out for recognition -- dragon-wrapped columns and hanging incense coils -- are both authored as real geometry rather than left to a material.
Action readiness is minimal: static landmark geometry, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Three repetition systems and two hand-built swept surfaces against a twelve-draw-call ceiling. The eleven incense coils alone would be eleven of the twelve as separate meshes.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: heavy low hip roof, CONCAVE in section -- steep at the ridge, flaring shallow at the eaves
two curled ridge ends and four flying eaves corners
gilt dragons coiling up the two centre front columns
eleven conical incense coils hung across the open front at staggered heights
stone drum base under every column
tripod stone censer standing on the porch floor
a pair of guardian beasts on the ridge
the dark face the open colonnade looks into
brown staining along the plinth edge, fading out by 0.75 m

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns: The rear and both short elevations are authored as plain red lacquer. The plate shows one closed elevation and it is plain; the others are unseen.

The roof tiles are individually laid half-round pantiles in the plate, ending in a stamped end-cap at every eaves course. The model carries a smooth swept surface. This is the largest departure from the plate and is reported as a risk.
TWO dragon columns, on the two centre front columns. The plate shows exactly two and the rest plain, which is the usual arrangement.
The guardian beasts on the ridge are blocked in as two silhouettes rather than sculpted. At the distance a shrine roof is read from they ARE two silhouettes.

The interior is not modelled. What the porch looks into is a single dark face on a solid body -- this prop is an exterior shell, and an interior would cost draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees.
preSpecAssessment.unknownsResolutionNote: Emptied because every entry has been RESOLVED with a recorded authoring decision, not because the gaps went away. Each is restated in assumptions and in viewEvidence with its confidence and a null path. Nothing was invented to close a gap.

definitionOfDone: Rendered model matches the reference silhouette, the 10.00 x 8.00 x 12.00 m proportions, the visible component hierarchy and the material response for a real-time browser prop.
All four scene-budget ceilings hold: <=16000 triangles, <=12 draw calls, <=8 materials, <=32 unique geometries.
Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

pivotInventory.name: root
pivotInventory.justification: The ONLY mechanism this prop has. Static landmark geometry: nothing opens, turns or swings, so every part is fixed and gets no axis. A named pivot is a promise that a part turns on it.

actionReadiness.socketJustification: ZERO sockets, deliberately. Nothing attaches to this prop and nothing is emitted from it. A marker named for a place on the surface is a location, not a mechanism.

colliderInventory.note: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the shrine, not with its individual columns.

actionReadiness.destructionJustification: The asset declares destructionGroups as an empty list -- this prop is NOT breakable. No component carries actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup. promote-model checks built against declared as an equality in BOTH directions, so an invented group fails the gate just as a missing one would.

assumptions: The rear and both short elevations are authored as plain red lacquer. The plate shows one closed elevation and it is plain; the others are unseen.

The roof tiles are individually laid half-round pantiles in the plate, ending in a stamped end-cap at every eaves course. The model carries a smooth swept surface. This is the largest departure from the plate and is reported as a risk.
TWO dragon columns, on the two centre front columns. The plate shows exactly two and the rest plain, which is the usual arrangement.
The guardian beasts on the ridge are blocked in as two silhouettes rather than sculpted. At the distance a shrine roof is read from they ARE two silhouettes.

coordinateFrame.notes: Origin base-center as the asset declares, +Y up. The OPEN FRONT faces +X, which is the long 12 m elevation, and that was a correction rather than a choice: built first with the porch on the short end, the band table read the body 0.47 of height too wide in every band from 1 to 4. The declared 10 x 12 makes this prop deeper than it is wide and the plate shows the opposite -- a shrine WIDER than deep, with its colonnade along the long face. The declared envelope is kept and the building is turned inside it.

silhouette.description: A low pale plinth, a red body barely half the plinth's depth with a deep open porch in front of it, and a roof that is nearly half the prop's height and wider than everything under it. The silhouette events are all in the roof: the concave sweep from a steep ridge out to shallow flaring eaves, the four corners curling up, and the two ridge-end curls.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -5.00..+5.00 = 10.00 and z spans -6.00..+6.00 = 12.00, both set by the bottom plinth slab; the roof reaches 9.10 m across at the eaves and its four upswept corners take it to exactly 10.00. y spans 0.00 to 8.00, the tip of a ridge-end curl. The plinth and the roof are the two parts that carry the declared envelope, and the building standing between them is deliberately smaller than either.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate normalises to long:h:short = 1 : 0.764 : 0.731 against the declared 1 : 0.667 : 0.833 -- the reference is taller and NARROWER than the declaration. After correcting the axis convention, area-weighted band comparison gives mean |delta width| 0.157 and |delta depth| 0.116 of height. Two rounds of rebuilding got it there. The first put the porch on the short elevation, which read +0.47 of height too wide through the body; the second still had the body filling the declared width, which read +0.34. The body and porch were then sized off the BAND TABLE rather than off the envelope, at 5.7 m deep, and bands 1 to 4 came in to +0.09. What is left is concentrated in exactly two bands -- band 0, the plinth, and bands 5 to 6, the roof eaves -- which are the two parts that carry the declared 10 x 12. The declaration is wider and squatter than the plate's object; it wins, and the difference is reported rather than split.

viewEvidence.note: NOT DIRECTLY OBSERVED. Confidence 0.60: the roof is four-fold in its construction and the plate shows two of its faces, but the BUILDING under it is not symmetric front to back -- it has one open elevation and three closed ones -- so the rear is authored as plain red lacquer with no way to check it.

componentTree.name: Stone plinth and censer
componentTree.topologyRationale: Two stepped slabs and the tripod censer standing on them, all the same stone and therefore ONE component and ONE draw call. The censer is freestanding in the plate and could have been its own component; it is not, because grouping by MATERIAL rather than by object is what holds the draw-call count down.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Two slabs to y=0.75 carrying the declared 10 x 12 footprint, plus a five-part tripod censer on the porch floor.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The two slabs meet top-to-bottom, which is an opposed butt, and the censer stands on the upper slab rather than in it.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Weathered granite, roughness 0.93, no texture set.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the shrine, not with its individual columns.

componentTree.name: Shrine body
componentTree.topologyRationale: A SOLID red mass filling the back of the plan, with the porch left open in front of it. The shrine is an exterior shell only ever seen from outside, so there is no interior; a solid body also means the porch needs no opening cut in it.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Solid box, x -3.60..+0.20, y 0.75..4.50, z +-4.40 -- 5.7 m deep against a 10 m plinth, because the reference reads the building at 0.60 of height where a body filling the declared width measured 0.96.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Stands clear of the plinth edge on every side and clear of the column line in front.

geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: PROUD of the red body, not recessed into it: the body is a solid mass, so a panel sunk into it is inside the solid and invisible.

componentTree.name: Gilt dragon spirals
componentTree.topologyRationale: The registry notes name the dragon-wrapped columns as one of the two features that carry recognition from outside, so the dragon is GEOMETRY and not a texture: a painted dragon needs the procedural texture set, which forces color to white and discards every measured albedo on the prop. Fifty-two short segments across two columns, merged into one component and one draw call.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A gilt spiral of 3.2 turns coiling up each of the two centre front columns.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Each segment is aimed along its own helical tangent by two Euler turns, so no two are parallel and nothing inside the merge can share a plane.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Gilt carving, roughness 0.40, metalness 0.30 -- below physical because the harness supplies no environment map.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Glazed tile roof
componentTree.topologyRationale: The whole identity of the prop, and everything green rides ONE component and ONE draw call: the hip surface, the ridge bar, its two curled ends, the four flying eaves corners and the pair of guardian beasts. It is generated as a ring of EIGHT-point rectangles climbing from the eaves to the ridge -- not an extrusion, which gives vertical gable ends, and not four points, which is what built a saddle.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: A concave hip roof from eaves at 4.50 to a ridge at 7.00, spanning 9.10 m at the eaves and 10.00 m at the lifted corners.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Closed as a SOLID -- outer surface, a soffit 0.34 m below the eaves and a fascia band between them. An open shell lets the turntable gate read straight through the roof from any low angle. The ring winding is counter-clockwise seen from above; wound the other way the whole roof renders inside out, which looks like a thin black membrane rather than a mistake.

localFeatures.delivery: hipRoof() with a shrink exponent above one

localFeatures.description: curled ridge ends and eaves corners

attachment.notes: The roof seats on the wall head at y=4.50 and embeds 0.20 m into it rather than resting on its top plane, so the two never share a surface. gapTolerance 0.01 m is the same tolerance check-coplanar runs at.

localOverrides.evidence: The plate's plinth is stained brown along its top edge and cleaner below. Delivered as a per-vertex TINT on the merged plinth geometry -- (0.86, 0.86, 0.84) at y=0 fading out by y=0.75 -- rather than as a second material, which would cost a draw call and a shader switch for a gradient.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-plinth (PBR confidence 0.841) on the porch floor.
Shared by the plinth, the tripod censer and the seven column drum bases -- three consumers, one stone.
Textureless: the plate's brown staining along the plinth edge is wear at a frequency no prop-distance viewer resolves, and only its vertical gradient is carried, as a vertex tint.
textureless.note: Declared textureless so createSculptMaterial skips makeProceduralTextureSet entirely -- FIVE canvases per material written pixel by pixel, at a cost that is the SQUARE of the resolution. It is also a correctness fix: with a texture set the generator forces color to white and roughness to 1 and reads both from the generated maps, discarding this measured albedo.

evidence: Measured on viewEvidence region-column (PBR confidence 0.761) at #421915 and LIFTED to #7E3029. The measured value is luma 45 against the harness backdrop's 58, and the silhouette gate classifies background by mean luma alone -- a whole red body below the backdrop value is read as a hole punched through the prop rather than as a wall. A deliberate deviation from the measurement, recorded with its reason and its margin: the shipped value is luma 71.

The narrow crop is why this is the lowest confidence of the six. A 16-pixel column strip returned 0.690, below the 0.7 threshold and therefore a stop signal rather than a pass; widening the crop to 30 pixels moved it to 0.761 without moving the surface it sits on.

repetitionSystems.name: Round columns

placement.note: Five along the front at x=1.90 and two returning at x=0.85, all on the open +X elevation.

repetitionSystems.rationale: Seven columns at one geometry and one submission against a twelve-draw-call ceiling.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The capital block is sunk 0.16 m into the shaft rather than sitting on it, so no two top faces share a plane inside the merged unit.

repetitionSystems.name: Column drum bases

placement.note: One under each column, on the same schedule.

repetitionSystems.rationale: A SECOND system on the same placement rather than a second colour on the first: InstancedMesh takes one material, and a stone base is a different SHAPE as well as a different stone, so a per-instance colour could not have carried it.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The drum is a wider cylinder under a narrower collar, so the two meet as opposed faces, and the column shaft starts above the collar.

repetitionSystems.name: Hanging incense coils

placement.note: Spread across the open front at three staggered heights and two staggered depths, so the cluster reads as a hanging field rather than a row.

repetitionSystems.rationale: The second of the two features the registry notes call out. Eleven cones at ONE geometry and one draw call; as separate meshes they would be eleven of the twelve draw calls available.
repetitionSystems.zFightingNote: The z spread was pulled in from +-3.55 to +-3.46 after check-coplanar found the outermost coil sharing its bounding plane with the outermost column base over 0.17 m2 -- two parts that never touch, flagged because their envelopes happened to align.

featureReviews.evidence: A hip roof sloping on all four sides, concave in section, from eaves at 4.50 m to a ridge at 7.00 m, spanning 9.10 m at the eaves and 10.00 m at the lifted corners.
featureReviews.notes: The registry notes open with a warning rather than a description -- it must not be built with the profile of a Thai wat -- and this roof is the opposite of one in three ways: hipped rather than gabled, low rather than steep, concave rather than straight. No existing helper could express it. It is generated directly as a ring of rectangles climbing from the eaves to the ridge, and the concavity comes from a horizontal shrink of (1-t)^q with q ABOVE one. The first attempt used q below one and built a flat-topped tent: slope is dy/dx, so a plan that shrinks fast for a given rise is a SHALLOW slope, and q>1 puts the fast shrink at the eaves where it belongs. The roof is also closed as a solid -- outer surface, soffit and fascia -- because an open shell lets the turntable gate read straight through it from any low angle.

featureReviews.evidence: Gilt dragons of 3.2 turns coiling up the two centre front columns as 52 tangent-aligned segments, and eleven conical incense coils hung at staggered heights and depths across the open front.
featureReviews.notes: Both are the features the registry notes name as carrying recognition from outside, so both are GEOMETRY. A painted dragon would need the procedural texture set, which forces color to white and roughness to 1 and would discard every measured albedo on the prop. The coil spread was pulled in from +-3.55 to +-3.46 after check-coplanar found the outermost coil sharing its bounding plane with the outermost column base over 0.17 m2 -- two parts that never touch, flagged because their envelopes happened to align.

featureReviews.evidence: Two curled ridge ends and four flying eaves corners, all merged into the single roof component, with the eaves staying down between the corners.
featureReviews.notes: The corner upsweep needed EIGHT points per ring rather than four. With four -- just the corners -- the lift had nowhere to fall away to and raised the entire eaves line, which built a saddle instead of a roof; the four edge midpoints are what hold the eaves down between the corners. The ring winding also had to be counter-clockwise seen from above: wound the other way the whole roof rendered inside out, which looks like a thin black membrane and reads as a material problem rather than a winding one.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Five components and three repetition systems: 8 of 12, the tightest draw-call headroom of the monumental set. The whole roof -- surface, ridge, four eaves curls, two ridge curls and two beasts -- is ONE submission, and the fifty-two dragon segments are another.

materials.note: pale covers the plinth, the censer AND the seven drum bases; red covers the body and the seven column shafts. Six of eight materials, two in hand -- the closest to its material ceiling of any prop here, and every one of the six is a genuinely different finish.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: 3,482 of 16,000. The roof sweep is the only expensive thing on the prop and it is cheap: nine rings of eight points is 144 quads. The headroom could buy the individual pantile course the plate shows and is deliberately not spent on it.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: A swept hip surface, a helix, curled horns and boxes. The roof is the one shape in this batch that no existing helper could express -- not an extrusion, which gives vertical gable ends, and not a lathe, which cannot be rectangular in plan -- so it is generated directly as a ring of eight-point rectangles climbing from the eaves to the ridge.

Three InstancedMesh systems carry 25 of the prop's 40 discrete parts. Two of them share one placement schedule and differ only in material and shape, which is what a column and its stone base actually are.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless and no canvas is generated at all. The individual pantile course and its stamped eaves end-caps are what is genuinely lost, and that is reported as this prop's largest risk.

risks.description: THREE of the six measured albedos ship above their measurements -- the red lacquer, the porch shade and the incense coils -- because all three fell at or below the harness backdrop's luma of 58.
risks.mitigation: This plate is a shaded shrine photographed under a deep overhang, and all three surfaces sit ENCLOSED by the prop's own outline, so at their measured values the silhouette gate reads them as holes punched through the building. The coil is the sharpest case: measured luma 57, one below the backdrop. Each lift records the measurement it departs from and the margin it ships at.

risks.description: The plate's roof is individually laid half-round pantiles with a stamped end-cap at every eaves course; the model carries a smooth swept surface.
risks.mitigation: The only route to it is the procedural texture set, which forces color to white and roughness to 1 and would discard all six measured albedos. Roughness 0.68 -- the tightest non-metal on the prop -- is how the glaze survives instead. Reported as the largest departure from the plate.

risks.description: The declared 10 x 8 x 12 is wider and squatter than the plate's object, and the residual band divergence sits entirely in the plinth and the roof eaves.
risks.mitigation: Those two components are what carry the declared envelope; the building between them was sized off the band table instead and matches to 0.09 of height. The declaration wins and the difference is reported.
